title: This Three-Meter Worm Slices Fish in Half From the Sand

scenes.text: This worm can slice a fish in half.
It's the bobbit worm, up to three meters long, buried deep in the seafloor.
Only its feelers stick out, waiting for something to swim past.
Then it lurches out like a coiled spring and snaps its jaws shut.
The strike can be so ferocious that the prey is sliced in half.
It drags the catch back to its burrow. One strike, and the fish is gone.

description:
A bobbit worm can slice a fish in half.
It grows up to three meters long, hides in the seafloor with only its feelers showing, and lurches out like a coiled spring when prey swims by.
Would you swim over sand after this?
first_comment: Worm, shark or snake: which ambush predator would you least want to meet?
